sections.h2: Where is Salt Lake City, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Salt Lake City is Utah's capital and the county seat of Salt Lake County. It covers about 110.8 square miles in the northeast corner of the Salt Lake Valley, between the Wasatch Range on the east and the Oquirrh Mountains on the west, with the Great Salt Lake to the northwest.

Elevation averages 4,327 feet, and the Jordan River runs through the city. Wikipedia describes the eastern neighborhoods, such as the Avenues, 9th and 9th, Yalecrest, Federal Heights and Sugar House, as tending to be more affluent. The western side, including Poplar Grove, Rose Park and Glendale, tends to be more working-class and ethnically diverse.

That east and west split is useful for sellers. A house in Yalecrest and a house in Rose Park can sit in very different neighborhoods, so it helps to know which side of the city yours is on.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Salt Lake City's older housing?
sections.html:
Salt Lake City was settled in 1847 by Latter-day Saint pioneers led by Brigham Young, incorporated in 1851 and platted in 1857. It was first named Great Salt Lake City, and the word Great was dropped in 1868.

A rail line reached the city in 1870, and Utah became a state in 1896 with Salt Lake City as its capital. The Avenues is a historic district with many Victorian-era homes. Older houses can need more upkeep, and some owners decide a cash sale is easier than managing a long repair list.

sections.h2: What does the Wasatch Fault mean for a Salt Lake City house?
sections.html:
The Wasatch Fault runs along the mountain front and the Salt Lake City segment sits under the city. Wikipedia reports that this segment last produced a major earthquake about 1,200 to 1,300 years ago.

The same page cites an estimated 57 percent chance of a magnitude 6.0 or greater earthquake within 50 years, and notes that surface rupture could shift the ground by as much as 20 feet. A magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna on March 18, 2020 caused damage across the valley.

  • At least 42 percent of Wasatch Front buildings are at risk of moderate to severe damage in a strong quake.
  • Liquefaction is a risk where buildings sit on soft lake sediments.
  • Damage to gas, electric and water lines is also expected after a large quake.

None of this stops a sale, but a house with visible damage from the 2020 quake or from settling is often easier to sell as-is than to repair first.

sections.h2: What are Salt Lake City's climate and air quality issues?
sections.html:
Salt Lake City has a humid continental climate with cold winters and hot summers. The airport averages about 15.5 inches of precipitation a year and roughly 52 inches of snow, and about 127 days a year drop to freezing or below.

Mean daily highs are 38.6 degrees in January and 94.0 degrees in July. Winter temperature inversions trap pollution in the valley, and the American Lung Association ranked the city sixth-worst for air quality in 2016.

For a house, the freeze count is the practical number. Roofs, gutters, sprinkler lines and exposed pipes all see repeated freeze and thaw, so a seller who has deferred roof or plumbing work may find buyers wary.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Salt Lake City, and who buys homes there?
sections.html:
The largest employer in Salt Lake City is the Delta hub at Salt Lake City International Airport. Other major employers include Intermountain Healthcare, the University of Utah, Sinclair Oil and the LDS Church, according to Wikipedia.

The city's daytime population is above 315,000, which is well over the resident count. Westminster University and Salt Lake Community College are also based in the city. Zions Bancorporation and Questar Corporation are headquartered here, and the city was selected to host the 2034 Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Transit adds to the picture. TRAX light rail opened in 1999, and the S Line streetcar, formerly the Sugar House Streetcar, opened in December 2013.

sections.h2: Do landlords in Salt Lake City need a license?
sections.html:
Yes. Every residential rental property inside Salt Lake City limits needs its own current business license, according to the city's Business Licensing page.

The Landlord/Tenant Initiative, also called the Good Landlord Program, applies to single and double family homes and similar rentals. The city says taking part can reduce per-unit licensing fees by up to 95 percent, and the program's ordinance took effect on September 1, 2011.

This matters if you inherited a house that was a rental, or if you own a duplex you no longer want to manage. A cash buyer can take the property with tenants in place, and you can ask what that would mean for the lease and your license.

sections.h2: What are the short-term rental rules in Salt Lake City?
sections.html:
Short-term rentals in Salt Lake City require a business license and are allowed only in approved zoning districts. A licensee may hold only one short-term rental license in the city.

  • Each license covers one property and one dwelling unit.
  • Stays must be at least two consecutive nights.
  • Each licensed unit is limited to 200 rental nights per calendar year.
  • Owners of buildings with more than 11 units may license up to 10 percent of the units.
  • Condominium units need an HOA authorization letter.

The city's page lists the approved districts, such as MU2, MU3, D1 and GMU, so check the zoning of your address before you count on short-term rental income in a sale. For fees and dates, the city refers callers to Business Licensing at (801) 535-7980.

sections.h2: How does property tax work in Salt Lake City?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County bills Salt Lake City homes. Market value is set as of January 1, and a primary residence gets a 45 percent exemption on buildings and up to one acre of land under Utah's rules.

The Notice of Valuation and Tax Change arrives in late July. The county Board of Equalization accepts appeals from August 1 through September 15, or 45 days from the notice if that is later, and appeals need a BE01 form and evidence of value. Late appeals may be accepted until March 31 of the next year, but only on narrow grounds.

The county Treasurer says tax notices with amounts due must be mailed by November 1, and that taxes are due November 30. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on December 1 with a penalty of the greater of 2.5 percent or $10, which drops to the greater of 1 percent or $10 if paid by January 31. The Treasurer certifies delinquent taxes on March 15, and the tax sale is traditionally held on the fourth Thursday of May.

sections.h2: What should a Salt Lake City seller disclose?
sections.html:
Utah's standard purchase contract asks sellers to disclose known problems, and the usual way to do that is a Seller's Property Condition Disclosure form. Ask your title or escrow company which disclosure forms apply to your sale.

The form covers roof leaks, flooding and drainage, mold, structural or soil problems, permits and HOA details. Because Utah has no exemption for inherited homes in that guide's description, heirs who never lived in the house should still describe what they know. When in doubt, ask a Utah real estate attorney.

The county Recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, keeps the property records, and its office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: Which way should a Salt Lake City seller go?
sections.html:
Salt Lake City sellers usually weigh a listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. The right choice depends on condition, timing and tenants.

A listing suits a well-kept house in a strong location where you can wait for showings. A cash sale suits a house with deferred repairs, a rental with tenants, a probate property or an owner who needs a specific closing date. You can request an offer, compare it with your likely net from a listing, and say no without owing anything.

faqs.q: What county is Salt Lake City in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Salt Lake City is also the county seat, so the county Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder serve its homeowners.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake City property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty is the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 per parcel, reduced to the greater of 1 percent or $10 if paid by January 31.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: September 15, or 45 days from the notice date if that is later. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization from August 1 and need a BE01 form with evidence supporting your value.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out my Salt Lake City house?
faqs.a: Yes. Every residential rental property in the city needs a valid business license for each location. The Good Landlord Program can cut per-unit fees by up to 95 percent.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Salt Lake City?
faqs.a: Only in approved zoning districts and with a city business license. Stays must be at least two nights, and each unit is capped at 200 rental nights a year.

faqs.q: Is earthquake risk a problem when selling a Salt Lake City house?
faqs.a: It can come up. The Wasatch Fault underlies the city, and buyers may ask about past damage. A cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands.
